problemStatement.formal: ∃ H : ℕ, ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ n ≥ N, primeGap n ≤ H (where primeGap n = p_{n+1} - p_n)
problemStatement.plain: There exists a constant H such that infinitely many pairs of consecutive primes differ by at most H. Zhang proved H ≤ 70M (2013), Maynard H ≤ 600 (2015), Polymath optimized to H ≤ 246 (2014).
whyMatters: Major breakthrough in analytic number theory (2013)
First proof of bounded gaps between primes

proven: Prime gap properties: positivity, evenness, ≥ 2 bound, g(0) = 1
Dickson conjecture implications for twin primes and triples

insights: Admissible tuples: H is admissible iff ∀ prime p, |H.image (· % p)| < p
Small primes checked by decide; large primes use |image| ≤ |H| < p
Maynard-Tao with m=2 gives bounded consecutive gaps
Prime gaps for n ≥ 1 are even (difference of two odd primes)
g(0) = 1 is the unique odd gap (p_0 = 2, p_1 = 3)
